ground_truth_witness: Take the two 7-cycles a = (0 1 2 3 4 5 6) and b = (0 1 2 3 4 6 5) in S_7 (as image tuples: a = (1,2,3,4,5,6,0), b = (1,2,3,4,6,0,5)). Both have cycle type (7), so both are genuine 7-cycles. Constructing the subgroup they generate by explicit breadth-first closure under composition inside S_7 gives |<a,b>| = 2520. Every element of the closure has sign +1 (exact inversion-count parity), so <a,b> <= A_7, and since |A_7| = 2520 = |<a,b>| we get <a,b> = A_7 exactly. The claim says |<a,b>| must be 7 (C_7), 168 (PSL(2,7)) or 5040 (S_7); here |<a,b>| = 2520, which is in none of those, so the trichotomy fails on this pair. Further witnesses with a = (0 1 2 3 4 5 6): b = (0 1 2 3 5 6 4), (0 1 2 3 5 4 6), (0 1 2 3 6 5 4), all giving order 2520.
ground_truth_flaw: The proof's Case 1 rests on the classification claim that a subgroup of S_7 generated by two 7-cycles must be C_7, PSL(2,7), or all of S_7. This trichotomy is false on both ends: S_7 can never arise (7-cycles are even, so the generated group lies in A_7), and the genuinely possible case A_7 is omitted from the enumeration.
